content.text: I'm examining a 5x5 grid where each 6 seems to get 2s placed at its orthogonal neighboring cells. The 6 at (3,3) already has its four neighbors marked with 2s, so I'm inferring that the 6 at (2,0), which is missing this pattern, should have 2s added at its own orthogonal neighbors.

content.text:
Testing the rule: each colored block cell spreads its marker value into its four orthogonal neighbors. Verifying against training examples confirms this pattern holds for both the 6 and 8 cases, so the output should be 8.

Now mapping this rule onto the test grid, I locate all the marker blocks (8s and existing 5s), then work out which block coordinates need to become 5 based on their adjacency to each 8. Translating block row/column positions into actual grid row/column ranges, I build out the full output grid block by block, leaving most rows empty except where 8s and their neighboring 5s appear.
